title: Telemetry huddle — weekly notes (tracing, dashboards, cost) 2026-03-22
content:
Purpose:
Weekly huddle notes for the observability team focused on tracing changes, dashboard cleanup, and cost telemetry experiments. Capture decisions, open questions, and action items for the next sprint.

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (owner)
- Ravi Kapoor
- Lina Gomez
- Ethan Park
- Sofia Alvarez
- Joined briefly: Tim O'Neill (infra), Priya S. (product)

Agenda:
1) Quick sync on last week's action items
2) Tracing sampling experiments and rollout plan
3) Dashboard consolidation and low-usage charts
4) Cost telemetry: per-model token attribution prototype
5) Incident postmortem follow-ups (latency spike on 2026-03-19)
6) AOB and blockers

Notes / Discussion:
- Tracing sampling: Ravi shared results from the two sampling strategies we ran on dedicated pools (adaptive reservoir vs fixed-rate). Adaptive reservoir preserved tail latency visibility for high-volume routes but increased ingestion costs by ~11% over baseline. Fixed-rate at 1% dropped observable slow-path traces for low-volume routes.
  - Decision: proceed with hybrid approach: adaptive reservoir for routes tagged "critical-path" + fixed-rate 0.5% for others for the next 2 weeks.
  - Follow-up: add a metric to dashboards showing "traces ingested per-route" to detect under-sampling.

- Dashboard cleanup: Lina presented usage stats pulled from telemetry-backend. 40% of dashboards haven't been viewed in 90 days; many panels redundant (same query, different time ranges). Team agreed on a lightweight retention policy: archive dashboards with <3 views and no owners after 30 days notice.
  - Concern: product teams sometimes rely on ad-hoc dashboards; plan to send a short notice email and create an "archived-dashboard" namespace in Confluence for quick restore.

- Cost telemetry: Ethan demoed the per-token attribution prototype that maps generation calls to model/route and attributes GPU-hours + S3 egress. Early numbers show a ~6% discrepancy vs billing (expected), mostly from intra-cluster caching not yet attributed.
  - Action: instrument prefix/KV cache hits with attribution tags (low-risk) to close the gap. Estimate: 2 days of dev + 1 day test.

- Incident follow-ups (2026-03-19 latency spike): postmortem draft (CONFLUENCE-OBS-INCIDENT-2026-03-19) shows cascade from a new kernel selection change on serving-runtime plus an overload on a single region fallback.
  - Mitigation implemented: automatic fallback throttling and a temporary kernel pin.
  - Long-term work: add a canary rollout for kernel selection changes (limiting to 2% traffic for 24 hours) and add a latency budget alert that triggers before error-rate alerts.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should sampling be to balance cost vs signal for AIOps? Need to surface observability ROI for top 10 routes to make a measured decision. (Owner: Maya; due 2026-03-29)
- Dashboard retention: who will be the single-point-of-contact for archival restoration requests? Suggestion: squads nominate owners; default to solutions-engineering if none. (Owner: Lina; due 2026-03-24)

Decisions made during the huddle:
- Hybrid tracing sampling rollout (adaptive reservoir for critical-path, fixed-rate 0.5% otherwise) for 2 weeks.
- Dashboard archival policy: <3 views & no owner -> archived after 30 days notice.
- Add canary rollout requirement to kernel selection PR checklist.

Action items (concrete):
- Ravi: implement hybrid sampling config in telemetry-agent and deploy to staging. Add metric: traces_ingested_per_route. (ETA: 2026-03-26)
- Lina: draft archive notice message and create "archived-dashboard" Confluence page with restore steps; coordinate with product mailing list. (ETA: 2026-03-24)
- Ethan: add attribution tags to prefix/KV cache hits; run reconciliation job against billing to measure remaining delta. (ETA: 2026-03-27)
- Maya: update kernel-selection PR checklist and write canary rollout guidance short doc; coordinate with serving-runtime owners. (ETA: 2026-03-29)
- Sofia: add a new Grafana panel to SRE dashboard showing traces_ingested_per_route and sampling rate by route. (ETA: 2026-03-26)

Blockers / Risks:
- Ingestion cost increase if adaptive sampling scales beyond initial traffic profile; need alerting on trace ingestion delta relative to baseline.
- Some product teams have opaque dashboard ownership; archival could remove useful views unexpectedly. Need communication plan.

Planned experiments next week:
- Run hybrid sampling on 2 non-production fleets and compare trace coverage on 2026-03-24 stress test. (Lead: Ravi)
- Run a 48h attribution reconciliation comparing prototype to billing for two high-volume customers. (Lead: Ethan)

Meeting artifacts and links:
- Postmortem draft: CONFLUENCE-OBS-INCIDENT-2026-03-19
- Sampling experiment results (internal sheet): github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-analysis/blob/main/sampling-experiments-2026-03.csv
- Dashboard usage spreadsheet: CONFLUENCE-DASHBOARD-OWNERSHIP-2026
- Kernel selection PR checklist (WIP): github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pulls/497

Next meeting:
- Weekly telemetry huddle, 2026-03-29, 10:00am PT. Focus: rollout results, cost delta, readiness to expand hybrid sampling.

Notes to self:
- Prioritize small, observable changes for tracing sampling so we can quickly rollback if ingestion spikes.
- Keep messaging short when archiving dashboards; include restore link and contact info.

---
